summary: Become variables (ansible_become, _method, _user, _password, _exe, _flags) replace the old sudo/su ones, and ansible_shell_type should only be changed when the shell executable is non-sh like csh or fish.
questions: How do I set the sudo user per host in inventory?
Where can I set become flags globally?
Should I set the sudo password in inventory?

answer_card.title: Privilege escalation and shell type variables
answer_card.answer_md:
- `ansible_become`: force escalation (old `ansible_sudo`/`ansible_su`).
- `ansible_become_method`: which become plugin.
- `ansible_become_user`: user to become.
- `ansible_become_password`: escalation password. **Always vault it.**
- `ansible_become_exe`, `ansible_become_flags`: executable and flags (flags can also go in `become_flags` under `[privilege_escalation]` in ansible.cfg).

`ansible_shell_type`: leave alone unless `ansible_shell_executable` is a non-sh shell; set to `csh` or `fish` so commands use that syntax.
